game.name: Deflector
game.short_description: Deflector is a top down action rogue-lite set in a deadly microcosm. Dive deep into hostile worlds teeming with viruses. Strike down increasingly challenging enemies with your weapons and their own deflected projectiles. Live, die, grow stronger and become powerful enough to reach the Source!

placements.verbal_evidence: "I'm going to leave it as a high the highest of be tiers and this is an easy a if it gets like a nice update"

commentary.label: Tier list Part 2 (2024)
commentary.summary: Deflector is a straightforward top-down action bullet-hell roguelike whose twist is a deflect button that differs per character and only works on red (and yellow) bullets. He finds the core gameplay very fun, clear and readable, but feels its late-run pacing suffers from multiple waves in large levels and that it lacks content and unique events. He hesitated between high B and low A and placed it at the top of B, saying an update could easily push it to A.
praise: Very readable, fast-paced gameplay with minimal mechanics and simple color-coded bullets
Each character's deflect is different and characters play very differently
Viable build paths: defensive, basic-attack or deflect-focused, despite modest upgrades
Smart difficulty scaling: four fixed worlds, choose three, each run gives worlds unique downsides so you must play all of them
criticism: Later runs have multiple waves per level and large maps, hurting the otherwise fast pacing
Hunting the last stray enemy in a corner slows things down even with a guiding arrow
Too few unique encounters; mostly shop, challenge and little else
Wants more mini-bosses, elites and general content, more bosses after finishing all characters
Upgrades are not hugely impactful; focus is on core gameplay over builds
unique_points: Per-character deflect mechanic restricted to certain bullet colors keeps the concept simple
Difficulty scaling via per-run world downsides rather than flat enemy stat increases
Gameplay-first design as the opposite approach to item-driven games like Binding of Isaac
commentary.quote: the gameplay is really really really solid
design_criteria: Readability/visual clarity: simple bullet colors make a fast game easy to track
Core gameplay feel: fast, satisfying deflect-based combat
Character diversity: each character and deflect plays differently
Build variety: upgrades modest but enable defensive, attack or deflect strategies
Pacing: multiple waves in large levels and straggler enemies drag late runs
Content variety: lacks unique events, elites and mini-bosses
Boss design: bosses praised but wants more
Difficulty scaling: world-specific downsides per run praised over flat stat increases
commentary.rerank_note: Not a re-rank, but he says it could move from top of B to an easy A with a good content/pacing update.

community.one_liner: A top-down action roguelite by Arrowfist Games in which you play a bioengineered 'Bioshell' inside a microscopic viral world and turn enemy projectiles (and your own) back on enemies by deflecting them.
community.consensus_summary: Deflector is well liked but niche: Steam shows 87% positive (Very Positive) from roughly 355 reviews, and the few critics who covered it were positive (Keengamer 8/10, Nine Over Ten 9/10, NaviGames 9/10, GameGrin 90). Praise centres on the deflect mechanic, build variety, the soundtrack and the Hades-like visual polish. The recurring complaints are a thin story, a fairly conventional roguelite loop and a lot of systems to track. It launched in Early Access on Jan 27, 2022 and hit 1.0 on Mar 24, 2023, with Switch and Xbox ports from Sept 2023 (PS4 listed on Metacritic). Its audience is small (estimated 20k-50k owners, about $113k gross), so there is little large-scale community discussion beyond Steam.
best_things: The deflect mechanic turns bullet-hell defence into offence: bouncing projectiles back at enemies, sometimes for huge damage, feels satisfying and skill-based
Real build variety from a free-form upgrade/mutation system where skills combine (for example clones, duplicated deflected shots, ground rupture)
Multiple Bioshell characters with different weapons and deflect behaviour, from the starting boomerang-wielding Eradicator to ranged and melee options
Strong soundtrack, praised by reviewers and Steam players
Polished stylised visuals, compared favourably to Hades in early coverage
Fast runs and non-linear path choices (combat, shops, rest areas) keep the pace brisk
Runs well, including on Steam Deck, with full controller support and plenty of achievements
worst_things: Story is barebones: a cool premise in the intro with little elaboration afterwards
Core roguelite structure is seen as conventional; critics say it does not reinvent the genre beyond deflection and setting
Some players call it a clunky Hades-like without enough of its own hook
Too many systems and modifiers to keep track of for some newcomers
Environment variety was criticised in early access and choosing locations had little gameplay impact
Only the starting character is available at first, so the early hours limit playstyle choice
Metacritic user reviewers (only 7 ratings) cite repetitiveness and limited enemy variety
improvements: Flesh out the narrative and world beyond the opening (raised by early access and 1.0 reviewers and Steam players)
Make location choices matter more to gameplay, not only to level progression
Add more visual and environmental variety across worlds
Give clearer objectives and clearer explanation of the many systems and modifiers
Unlock additional Bioshells faster or more clearly so early runs have more variety
unique_things: Deflection as the core verb: you can reflect enemy projectiles and your own weapon shots back for damage
Microscopic viral setting where you play as a prototype cure, with 'Apex Virus' bosses ending each world
Pitched by the developer as Diablo meets bullet hell, blending ARPG build crafting with bullet-hell patterns
Free-form skill combination system in which upgrades stack into unexpected effects
Hub with research modules and DNA/mutation progression that persists between runs
tedious_or_disliked: Gradual unlock of Bioshells and mutations requires repeated runs before the game opens up
Keeping track of numerous upgrades, modifiers and interactions is tiring for some players
Story and objectives give little incentive to push on for players not hooked by the combat
Runs can feel repetitive with limited enemy variety (Metacritic user ratings, small sample)
divisive_points: Originality: some critics and players call it a fresh take on bullet-hell roguelites, others say it does nothing special beyond deflection
Complexity: many enjoy the deep build-crafting, while others feel overloaded by what they must track
Value: a Metacritic user complaint mentions a steep price drop shortly after launch, which soured some buyers
community.reception_notes: Metacritic has no Metascore yet (needs 4 critic reviews; GameGrin 90 and KeenGamer 80 are listed) and its user score of 4.1/10 rests on only 7 ratings, so it is not meaningful. OpenCritic lists 4 reviews but no aggregate average on the page (scored ones average about 7.6/10). Early Access coverage from But Why Tho and Rock Paper Shotgun was unscored and positive about the mechanic and visuals. 1.0 launched Mar 24, 2023 on Steam ($19.99, Windows only), followed by Switch and Xbox in Sept 2023. Steam review volume is low and recent reviews are still positive; SteamSpy-style estimates put owners at 20k-50k and gross revenue at about $113k (Boxleiter-based estimate, order of magnitude only). The game was also offered via a free demo (Specimen Zero) on Steam.
